schema_023: For these asset types, keep name references without expanding appearance; other types retain default expansion.
schema_025: Summarize the subject, core action and dramatic outcome in one directly generatable video description. When dialogue, narration or inner monologue carries key dramatic information, identify the voice and its purpose; do not use only abstract emotion or a plot title.
schema_026: Shot duration such as 3s, 4s or 8s, within 1–30 seconds.
schema_027: Shot size and camera position, such as frontal medium shot or over-the-shoulder.
schema_028: Visual style throughout the shot, not plot actions.
schema_029: Explicitly forbidden cheap or inappropriate effects for this genre.
schema_030: Time, weather and overall lighting conditions.
schema_031: Environmental state, light layers and atmospheric changes.
schema_032: Complete spatial relationships among characters, entrances, main fixtures and camera. Specify initial positions, orientation and action starts. Convert adjacent-shot continuity into concrete current-shot conditions.
schema_033: Core visual description. Reference registered entities with @{Full Entity Name}; never repeat their appearance. Describe unregistered objects in precise material, texture and micro-action detail.
schema_034: Timed actions in start-end: action form. Repeat the explicit subject in every range using @{Full Entity Name} for registered characters. Do not omit names or rely on contextual pronouns. Actions must be precise and physically coherent.
schema_035: Format and texture: include shutter angle, digital/film capture, grain and halation. Example: 180-degree shutter; digital capture emulating Kodak Vision3 500T; heavy film grain.
schema_036: Lenses and filters: include focal length, spherical/anamorphic lens type and diffusion/polarizing filters. Example: 35mm anamorphic, Black Pro-Mist 1/8, slight edge distortion.
schema_037: Lighting and atmosphere: key direction, key/fill ratio, bounce or negative fill and haze/mist. Example: Rembrandt lighting from camera right, volumetric haze, negative fill on the left.
schema_038: Grade and palette: specify highlight, midtone and shadow colors. Example: warm amber highlights, teal shadows and desaturated mids.
schema_039: Camera movement: use precise dolly, truck, pan, tilt, Steadicam or handheld terms with speed and stability. Example: slow push-in with subtle handheld movement.
schema_040: Diegetic sound only: include concrete loudness in LUFS, ambience and material friction. Example: heavy breathing at -15 LUFS, distant wind and footsteps on snow.
schema_041: Narration and inner monologue, each with precise start/end times, speaker, delivery and words. The selected strategy determines permission and timing relative to dialogue. Return an empty list when absent.
schema_042: Character dialogue with speaker, delivery and the intended words in the output language. Return an empty list when absent.
schema_043: Explain adjacent-shot continuity and the current shot's visible ending frame and cut point. Do not give only a non-executable instruction such as continue the preceding shot.
schema_044: Restrained permitted effects. When none are needed, explicitly request realistic natural-light photography.
schema_045: Internal cuts within the current generation request. Use only when needed; the renderer numbers them from 1.
schema_050: Speaking character IDs linked to assets.
schema_054: Original prompt read by the editor, used to prevent overwriting concurrent changes.
schema_058: Create a base character, location or prop setting.
schema_059: Chapter-specific variant of an existing character. The parent determines type; asset_type, aliases and is_global are not accepted.
schema_060: All asset types returned in one model response.
schema_064: Narrative identity or function in the task language.
schema_065: Stable visual description in the target prompt language.
schema_067: Stable location design in the target prompt language.
schema_069: Stable prop design in the target prompt language.

schema_078: Character personality, background, motives and arc in the task language.
schema_079: Detailed character appearance in the task language.

schema_082: Complete outline including the central conflict, major turns and ending direction.
schema_083: Key characters driving the main story, usually three to ten.
schema_084: Read current context and constraints. chapter_offset pages through text; changes_page pages through actual conversation receipts.

schema_088: Read the matching system rules before creation or a full rewrite. target also reads the actual object; its type determines the rules.

schema_090: Page through original conversation records or compacted references. History never replaces current objects or permissions.
schema_091: Replace exact prompt fragments in already-read settings or shots, retaining other content and returning reversible receipts.
schema_092: Create a character (1), location (2) or prop (3). First read get_creation_prompt_rules and provide a complete visual design; the server renders the reference task.
